segments.en: Hello English learners, welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 您好英语学习者，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: And today we're going to have a fun, funny lesson.
segments.zh: 今天我们要上一堂既有趣又好笑的课。

segments.en: So I think this lesson's going to be a little bit different than most of our lessons, right?
segments.zh: 所以我认为这节课会和我们的大部分课程有些不同，对吧？

segments.en: Today we're going to be looking at jokes, which is a very important part of English speaking culture.
segments.zh: 今天我们将看笑话，这是英语文化中非常重要的一部分。

segments.en: So we're actually, we're going to teach you a few pretty hilarious jokes, but we're also going to teach you some language related to jokes, funny things, and that sort of stuff.
segments.zh: 所以我们实际上，我们将教你一些非常搞笑的笑话，但我们也要教你一些与笑话、有趣的事情和诸如此类的东西相关的语言。

segments.en: So in order for us to understand a little bit better the jokes that we're going to be looking at, why don't we take a look at vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 所以为了让我们更好地理解我们将要看的笑话，我们为什么不看看词汇预览。

segments.en: Two of these words you'll hear in the dialogue, but one you won't, but you still need to know this word so you can understand the jokes.
segments.zh: 这些词里有两个你会在对话中听到，有一个不会，但你仍然需要知道这个词，这样你才能理解这些笑话。

segments.en: So the word that we're talking about is not really a word.
segments.zh: 所以我们所说的这个词并不是一个真正的词。

segments.en: So moo is the sound that cows make.
segments.zh: 所以 Moo 是奶牛发出的声音。

segments.en: I could do a good cow.
So we all know now that that's what cows say.
segments.zh: 所以我们现在都知道，这就是奶牛所说的。

segments.en: So it's going to be important for the joke.
Now another word that you need to understand is a dam.
segments.zh: 现在你需要理解的另一个词是大坝。

segments.en: A dam is like a big wall, right?
segments.zh: 大坝就像一堵大墙，对吧？

segments.en: Well, it's a wall in water that stops the river from flowing.
segments.zh: 好吧，它是一堵水中的墙，可以阻止河流流动。

segments.en: So usually you build dams in rivers and then the water can pass or not.
segments.zh: 所以通常你在河流中建造水坝，然后水可以通过或不通过。

segments.en: It's something that you use to generate electricity, right?
segments.zh: 这是你用来发电的东西，对吧？

segments.en: But there's another word that sounds exactly the same way, but it's just spelled a little differently.
segments.zh: 但是还有另一个词听起来完全相同，但拼写有点不同。

segments.en: And we might hear someone say, oh, damn.
segments.zh: 我们可能会听到有人说，哦，该死的。

segments.en: And that's an interjection, which basically means...
segments.zh: 这是一个感叹词，基本上意味着...

segments.en: So it's an interesting interjection and we'll also see it in one of our jokes.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个有趣的感叹词，我们也会在我们的一个笑话中看到它。

segments.en: And now let's move on to our last word.
segments.zh: 现在让我们继续看最后一个词。

segments.en: So a nostril or your nostrils.
The two holes in your nose.
So now that we've taken a look at these three words, why don't we listen to our comedian for the first time and then we'll come back and talk a little bit more.
segments.zh: 既然我们已经看了这三个词，我们为什么不先第一次听我们的喜剧演员表演，然后再回来多聊一点。

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to Open Mic Night.
segments.zh: 各位好，欢迎来到开放麦之夜。

segments.en: You're in for a real treat as we've got a lot of great comics here with us tonight.
segments.zh: 今晚有很多优秀的喜剧演员到场，大家可有眼福了。

segments.en: First up, we have a very funny man coming straight from the state of Montana, Robert Hicks.
segments.zh: 首先登场的是一位非常风趣的男士，来自蒙大拿州的罗伯特·希克斯。

segments.en: You know, there's nothing I love better than stand up comedy.
segments.zh: 你知道，没有什么比单口喜剧更让我喜欢的了。

segments.en: You know, I've been working on my routine for months now and I've got some real zingers for you tonight.
segments.zh: 这套段子我已经打磨好几个月了，今晚要给大家讲几个绝妙的笑话。

segments.en: Let's start out with some short jokes.
segments.zh: 让我们从一些简短的笑话开始。

segments.en: Where do you find a one-legged dog?
segments.zh: 到哪儿能找到一只只有一条腿的狗？
你把它放在哪儿，它就在哪儿。

segments.en: Anyways, what do you call a sheep with no legs?
segments.zh: 无论如何，你怎么称呼没有腿的羊？

segments.en: Now, you're going to love this joke.
segments.zh: 现在，你会喜欢这个笑话。

segments.en: What do cows do for entertainment?
We've got a few hecklers in the audience, but this one is good.
segments.zh: 观众里有人在起哄，不过下面这个笑话可不错。

segments.en: What does a fish say when it runs into a wall?
segments.zh: 鱼撞到墙上时会说什么？

segments.en: Why do gorillas have big nostrils?
segments.zh: 为什么大猩猩有大鼻孔？

segments.en: Okay, so some pretty hilarious jokes, huh?
segments.zh: 好吧，那么一些非常搞笑的笑话，对吧？

segments.en: I don't think the crowd really enjoyed them all that much.
segments.zh: 我觉得观众真的没那么喜欢这些笑话。

segments.en: Okay, well, maybe I'm just a fan of really terrible jokes.
segments.zh: 好吧，也许我只是一个非常糟糕的笑话的粉丝。

segments.en: Well, they were pretty funny, but I guess the crowd just didn't appreciate his sense of humor.
segments.zh: 嗯，这些笑话挺有趣的，但我想观众只是不欣赏他的幽默感。

segments.en: They did use quite a lot of really interesting language.
segments.zh: 他们确实使用了很多非常有趣的语言。

segments.en: So why don't we look at that now in Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不现在在语言要点中看一下。

segments.en: On Language Takeaway, we're going to be looking at six words today, so let's get started.
segments.zh: 关于语言要点，我们今天将查看六个单词，所以让我们开始吧。

segments.en: The announcer welcomed everyone and said that it's open mic night.
segments.zh: 播音员欢迎大家，说现在是开放式麦克风之夜。

segments.en: Okay, well, we know mic is short for microphone, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，我们知道 mic 是 microphone 的缩写，对吧？

segments.en: Now, an open mic night is a chance where anyone can come up and talk into the microphone.
segments.zh: 所谓开放麦之夜，就是任何人都可以上台对着麦克风说话的机会。

segments.en: So you can come up and sing or you can tell jokes, you can do anything, basically.
segments.zh: 所以你可以上来唱歌，或者你可以讲笑话，你可以做任何事情，基本上。

segments.en: So it's not for professionals, but for people who maybe want to be professionals.
segments.zh: 所以它不是为了专业人士，而是适合那些可能想成为专业人士的人。

segments.en: So it was open mic night and he said they had a lot of great comics there.
segments.zh: 所以这是开放麦之夜，他说现场来了很多很棒的喜剧演员。

segments.en: So basically, a comic is a person that makes a living by making people laugh.
segments.zh: 所以基本上，喜剧演员就是靠逗人发笑谋生的人。

segments.en: Yeah, someone who stands up on stage and tells jokes.
segments.zh: 是的，站在舞台上讲笑话的人。

segments.en: So, a clown is kind of like a comic?
segments.zh: 所以，小丑有点像喜剧演员吗？

segments.en: A comic doesn't wear a red nose and a crazy...
segments.zh: 喜剧演员不戴红鼻子，也不穿那些夸张的...

segments.en: Alright, yeah, because I hate clowns.
We do know that about you.
And well, what comics do is they perform stand-up comedy.
segments.zh: 嗯，喜剧演员做的就是表演单口喜剧。

segments.en: Okay, so stand-up comedy is really exactly what its name suggests, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，所以单口喜剧确实是它的名字所暗示的，对吧？

segments.en: Right, you stand up in front of an audience and you tell jokes or you make them laugh.
segments.zh: 是的，你站在观众面前，你讲笑话或让他们发笑。

segments.en: It's a very popular form of entertainment in the United States and the UK.
segments.zh: 在美国和英国，这是一种非常流行的娱乐形式。

segments.en: And I think we'll talk a little bit more about that at the end of the lesson, but why don't we move on to our next word, which is routine.
segments.zh: 我想我们会在课程结束时多聊一点，但我们为什么不接着看下一个词——routine。

segments.en: So the guy says, I've been working on my routine.
segments.zh: 所以那家伙说，我一直在打磨我的段子。

segments.en: So what does he mean by his routine?
segments.zh: 那他说的 routine 是什么意思呢？

segments.en: Well, I guess a routine is like a series or a collection of jokes or maybe movements that you use in a performance.
segments.zh: 我觉得 routine 就像一组或一系列笑话，也可能是你在表演里用到的一些动作。

segments.en: So you can talk about a dance routine.
segments.zh: 所以你可以谈论一个舞蹈套路。

segments.en: Or in this case, a comedy routine.
segments.zh: 或者在这种情况下，喜剧套路。

segments.en: So the series of jokes he's going to tell.
segments.zh: 所以他要讲的一系列笑话。

segments.en: That's right, that he practices again and again and again.
segments.zh: 没错，他一次又一次地练习。

segments.en: Alright, and in his routine, he said he's got a lot of zingers.
segments.zh: 好吧，在他的段子里，他说他有很多 zingers。

segments.en: Basically, a zinger is like a strong, maybe a little bit rude joke.
segments.zh: 基本上，zinger 就是一句犀利、可能还有点粗鲁的笑话。

segments.en: Yeah, but like a kind of a one-line joke, right?
segments.zh: 是的，但就像那种一句话的笑话，对吧？

segments.en: And the people that were in the crowd and they were booing him, they were like, boo, those we call hecklers.
segments.zh: 观众里有人在嘘他，就是那种“嘘”的声音，我们管这些人叫起哄者。

segments.en: And that's our last word, a heckler.
segments.zh: 这就是我们的最后一个词——heckler。

segments.en: So, let's listen to some hecklers in action.
segments.zh: 所以，我们来听听起哄者是怎么起哄的。

segments.en: Alright well, I think that's pretty clear.
So now that we've finished looking at all the words that are related to comedy and performances, let's take a look at the jokes now in Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 现在我们已经看完了所有与喜剧和表演有关的词，让我们在流利表达里来看看这些笑话。

segments.en: Okay, well we're not really focusing on new phrases for you here, but we thought it would be helpful to talk a little bit about the jokes to help you understand them, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，我们并没有真正专注于您的新短语，但我们认为稍微谈谈这些笑话以帮助您理解它们会有所帮助，对吧？

segments.en: Because they are, well, I think pretty funny.
segments.zh: 因为他们，嗯，我觉得很有趣。

segments.en: Yeah, they're pretty funny, but maybe sometimes they're kind of hard to understand.
segments.zh: 是的，它们很有趣，但有时它们可能有点难以理解。

segments.en: So why don't we start with the first joke?
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不从第一个笑话开始呢？

segments.en: So you said, where do you find a one-legged dog?
segments.zh: 所以你说，你在哪里找到一只腿的狗？
那么什么是一只腿的狗呢？

segments.en: Basically, it's a dog that has one leg.
segments.zh: 基本上，它是一条只有一条腿的狗。

segments.en: Ah, okay, and the pronunciation here is important, right?
segments.zh: 啊，好吧，这里的发音很重要，对吧？

segments.en: So you can say a one-legged dog, a two-legged dog, or a three-legged dog.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说一只单腿的狗、一只两腿的狗或一只三腿的狗。

segments.en: Maybe he lost two legs in a war.
segments.zh: 也许他在一场战争中失去了两条腿。

segments.en: Okay, so the dog obviously didn't go anywhere, and so that's why you find it where you left it.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这只狗显然哪儿也没去，这就是为什么你会在把它放下的地方找到它。

segments.en: So that's why it's kind of funny.
segments.zh: 所以这就是为什么它有点有趣。

segments.en: All right, so then he said, what do you call a sheep with no legs?
segments.zh: 好吧，然后他说，你怎么称呼没有腿的羊？

segments.en: A cloud, basically, because sheep are fluffy and they're white, so if you take away their legs, they look like a little cloud.
segments.zh: 云，基本上，因为羊很蓬松，而且它们是白色的，所以如果你把它们的腿拿走，它们看起来就像一团小云。

segments.en: All right, let's look at the next one.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们看看下一个笑话。

segments.en: He asked, what do cows do for entertainment?
segments.zh: 他问，奶牛为了娱乐做什么？

segments.en: And then the answer was, they rent movies.
segments.zh: 然后答案是，它们租电影。

segments.en: So it's kind of funny because he's relating this word movies with the sound that cows make, which is moo.
segments.zh: 所以这很有趣，因为他将这个词电影与奶牛发出的声音联系起来，这是哞哞。

segments.en: So there are a million jokes in English following the same pattern, right?
segments.zh: 所以有一百万个英语笑话遵循相同的模式，对吧？

segments.en: So I'm sure you can find a lot more of them and you can share them with us.
segments.zh: 所以我相信你可以找到更多的它们，你可以与我们分享。

segments.en: Now my personal favorite joke is, the guy says, what does a fish say when it runs into a wall?
segments.zh: 现在我个人最喜欢的笑话是，这家伙说，当鱼撞到墙上时，它会说什么？

segments.en: So to run into a wall, basically is, to crash against the wall.
segments.zh: 所以跑到墙上，基本上就是，撞到墙上。

segments.en: So what does the fish say?

segments.zh: 那么为什么这很有趣呢？

segments.en: Well, because, I mean, if you're a person and you run into a wall, damn, like, you know, it's like, oh no.
segments.zh: 好吧，因为，我的意思是，如果你是一个人，你撞到了墙上，该死的，就像，你知道，就像，哦不。

segments.en: But a fish is swimming under the water and like we saw, a dam is actually like a wall in the water.
segments.zh: 但是一条鱼在水下游泳，就像我们看到的那样，水坝实际上就像水中的一堵墙。

segments.en: So he's saying like, a wall.
The last one was pretty good.
Why do gorillas have big nostrils?
segments.zh: 为什么大猩猩有大鼻孔？

segments.en: Okay, so the big holes in their nose.
segments.zh: 好吧，他们鼻子上有大洞。

segments.en: And basically, it's because they have big fingers.
segments.zh: 基本上，这是因为他们有大手指。

segments.en: So they can put their fingers in the nose?
segments.zh: 那么他们可以把手指放在鼻子里吗？

segments.en: If the gorilla didn't have big nostrils, he wouldn't be able to pick his nose.
segments.zh: 如果大猩猩没有大鼻孔，他将无法挖鼻子。

segments.en: Maybe he'd have to use a stick.
segments.zh: 也许他必须用一根棍子。

segments.en: Yeah, but that wouldn't be convenient.
So that's why those jokes are funny.
segments.zh: 所以这就是为什么这些笑话很有趣。

segments.en: Of course, some of them are not actually really funny, but it's just a little bit of a taste of short American jokes.
segments.zh: 当然，其中一些其实没那么好笑，但这能让你稍稍尝到一点美式短笑话的味道。

segments.en: Okay, well, I think we need to hear them one more time in context so you can all know how funny or maybe not so funny they are.
segments.zh: 好吧，好吧，我认为我们需要在上下文中再听一次，这样你们才能知道他们有多有趣，或者可能不那么有趣。

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to Open Mic Night.
segments.zh: 各位好，欢迎来到开放麦之夜。

segments.en: You're in for a real treat as we've got a lot of great comics here with us tonight.
segments.zh: 今晚有很多优秀的喜剧演员到场，大家可有眼福了。

segments.en: First up, we have a very funny man coming straight from the state of Montana, Robert Hicks.
segments.zh: 首先登场的是一位非常风趣的男士，来自蒙大拿州的罗伯特·希克斯。

segments.en: You know, there's nothing I love better than stand-up comedy.
segments.zh: 你知道，没有什么比单口喜剧更让我喜欢的了。

segments.en: You know, I've been working on my routine for months now and I've got some real zingers for you tonight.
segments.zh: 这套段子我已经打磨好几个月了，今晚要给大家讲几个绝妙的笑话。

segments.en: Let's start out with some short jokes.
segments.zh: 让我们从一些简短的笑话开始。

segments.en: Where do you find a one-legged dog?
segments.zh: 到哪儿能找到一只只有一条腿的狗？
你把它放在哪儿，它就在哪儿。

segments.en: Anyways, what do you call a sheep with no legs?
segments.zh: 无论如何，你怎么称呼没有腿的羊？

segments.en: All right, now you're going to love this joke.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在你会喜欢这个笑话。

segments.en: What do cows do for entertainment?
We've got a few hecklers in the audience, but this one is good.
segments.zh: 观众里有人在起哄，不过下面这个笑话可不错。

segments.en: What does a fish say when it runs into a wall?
segments.zh: 鱼撞到墙上时会说什么？

segments.en: Why do gorillas have big nostrils?
segments.zh: 为什么大猩猩有大鼻孔？

segments.en: Thanks everyone, that was my time.
segments.zh: 谢谢大家，我的时间到了。

segments.en: Now if you have any good jokes of your own, why don't you come to our website and tell us about them.
segments.zh: 现在，如果您有自己的好笑话，为什么不来我们的网站告诉我们。

segments.en: Right, come to EnglishPod.com, share with us any jokes.
segments.zh: 对，来englishpod.com，与我们分享任何笑话。

segments.en: Of course, they have to be clean.
segments.zh: 当然，它们必须是干净的。

segments.en: All right, so we'll see you guys there and until next time.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们会在那里见到你们，直到下一次。
